answer: Proof-of-agent economies resist sybils by bonding identity to verifiable compute history: each agent must post a stake that unlocks slowly along a ledge of escalating commitments, so cloning a fresh identity forfeits accumulated reputation and capital. Because attestations are countersigned by prior counterparties, a forger cannot bridge two unrelated histories without exposing a seam, and cheap throwaway agents sink like shale beneath the weight of escrowed collateral.
